passages.p01: During hot weather, the body cools itself mainly by sweating. As sweat evaporates from the skin, it carries heat away. However, sweating also drains the body of water and salt. A person who exercises in the heat without drinking enough fluids can become dehydrated within an hour. Early signs include thirst, headache, and dark yellow urine. Because thirst often lags behind the body's actual need, people working outdoors are advised to drink water at regular intervals rather than waiting until they feel thirsty.
passages.p02: In April 1860, the Pony Express began carrying mail between St. Joseph, Missouri, and Sacramento, California. Riders changed horses at stations spaced along the nearly 2,000-mile route, and a letter could cross the distance in about ten days, far faster than by stagecoach. Despite its fame, the service lasted only about eighteen months. In October 1861, the transcontinental telegraph line was completed, and messages that once took days could be sent in minutes. The Pony Express, which had never been profitable, shut down soon after.
passages.p03: Most deaths from home fires happen at night, when people are asleep. Smoke detectors give early warning, but only if they work. Fire safety officials recommend testing each detector once a month by pressing its test button, replacing the batteries at least once a year, and replacing the entire unit every ten years. A detector with a dead battery offers no protection at all, yet many homes have at least one detector that does not work.
passages.p04: Many people believe that learning a second language is only possible in childhood. It is true that young children pick up pronunciation more easily. But adults have advantages of their own: they can study grammar in an organized way, use memory techniques, and connect new words to things they already know. Adults who practice regularly often make faster early progress than children do. Age, in other words, is a poor excuse for not starting.
passages.p05: Honeybees are best known for making honey, but their greatest value to people lies elsewhere. As bees move from flower to flower collecting nectar, they carry pollen that allows many plants to produce fruit and seeds. Crops such as almonds, apples, and blueberries depend heavily on bee pollination. For this reason, many farmers rent hives and place them in their orchards during the blooming season.
passages.p06: A compass needle points toward magnetic north, which is not the same as true north, the direction of the North Pole. The difference between the two, called declination, depends on where you are. In some places it is less than one degree; in others it is more than twenty. Military maps list the declination for the area they cover, so a soldier navigating with a map and compass must adjust each bearing by that amount. Ignoring declination can put a traveler hundreds of meters off course over a long march.
passages.p07: Adults who regularly sleep fewer than seven hours a night are more likely to have trouble concentrating, to get sick, and to be involved in accidents. Many people try to make up for lost sleep on weekends, but sleeping late on Saturday does not fully undo the effects of a week of short nights. Experts recommend going to bed and waking up at about the same time every day, even on days off.
passages.p08: NOTICE: Effective Monday, all personnel must sign out vehicles at the motor pool office before 0800. Vehicles must be returned with at least half a tank of fuel. Any damage must be reported on Form 12 before the driver leaves the lot. Drivers who do not follow these procedures will lose vehicle privileges for thirty days.
passages.p09: Lightning is a giant spark of electricity. It forms when ice particles and water droplets collide inside a storm cloud, building up electric charges. Because light travels much faster than sound, you see the flash before you hear the thunder. Counting the seconds between the two and dividing by five gives a rough distance to the strike in miles. If the count is thirty seconds or less, the storm is close enough to be dangerous, and you should seek shelter.
passages.p10: During World War II, the U.S. Marine Corps needed a way to send battlefield messages that the enemy could not understand. The answer came from Navajo servicemen, who developed a code based on their own language, which had no written form and was spoken by very few outsiders. Code talkers could encode, send, and decode a message in minutes, a task that took the coding machines of the time much longer. The code was never broken during the war.
passages.p11: A credit card can be a useful tool, but carrying a balance from month to month is expensive. If you owe $1,000 on a card with a 20 percent annual interest rate and pay only the minimum each month, it can take years to pay off the debt, and you may pay hundreds of dollars in interest along the way. Paying the full balance every month avoids interest charges entirely.
passages.p12: Before a hard workout, a proper warm-up raises body temperature and increases blood flow to the muscles. Five to ten minutes of light jogging or brisk walking, followed by movements that resemble the activity to come, prepares the body for effort and may reduce the risk of injury. Holding long stretches without moving, once standard advice before exercise, is now considered less useful than this kind of active warm-up.
passages.p13: Recycling an aluminum can saves about 95 percent of the energy needed to make a new can from raw ore. Aluminum can also be recycled again and again without losing quality. A can that is returned for recycling can be back on a store shelf as a new can in as little as two months.
passages.p14: In many small towns, there is no paid fire department. Instead, residents train in their spare time and answer calls at all hours, often leaving their jobs or families at a moment's notice. They receive little or no pay. Without these volunteers, many rural communities would have no fire protection at all, and their dedication deserves far more recognition than it usually gets.
passages.p15: Underinflated tires wear out faster, lower fuel economy, and make a vehicle harder to control. Because tires slowly lose air over time and in cold weather, drivers should check tire pressure at least once a month. The correct pressure is listed on a sticker inside the driver's door. The number printed on the side of the tire is the maximum pressure the tire can safely hold, not the recommended pressure.
passages.p16: Some kinds of bamboo can grow more than two feet in a single day, making bamboo one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth. Despite its treelike height, bamboo is actually a type of grass. Its strength and rapid growth have made it a popular building material in many parts of Asia, where it is used for scaffolding, floors, and furniture.
passages.p17: Maria wanted to save money for a car. Each week, she put half of her paycheck into a savings account. She stopped buying lunch and started packing food from home. After one year, she had saved enough to buy a used car.
passages.p18: Dogs pant to cool down. Unlike people, dogs have very few sweat glands in their skin. When a dog pants, water evaporates from its tongue and mouth, and that carries heat away from its body.
passages.p19: The town library will be closed on Monday for the holiday. It will open again on Tuesday at 9:00 a.m. Books that are due on Monday may be returned on Tuesday without a late fee.
passages.p20: Many people think bats are blind, but this is not true. All bats can see. Many bats also use echolocation: they make high-pitched sounds and listen for the echoes to find insects in the dark.
passages.p21: Sergeant Lee told the recruits to drink water before the march, even if they were not thirsty. "By the time you feel thirsty," she said, "your body is already low on water."
passages.p22: Wearing a seat belt is one of the most effective ways to reduce injuries in a car crash. A seat belt keeps you from being thrown against the dashboard or out of the vehicle. Buckling up takes only a few seconds.
passages.p23: Honey almost never spoils. It contains very little water and is naturally acidic, so bacteria have a hard time growing in it. Kept in a sealed jar, honey can last for many years.
passages.p24: The new gym on base is open from 5:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. every day. Service members may bring one guest. Guests must be at least 16 years old and must sign in at the front desk.
passages.p25: Kevin failed his first driving test because he forgot to signal before changing lanes. He practiced with his uncle every weekend for a month. On his second try, he passed easily.
passages.p26: Volunteers planted 200 trees in the park last Saturday. The trees will provide shade in the summer and help keep soil from washing away when it rains. The city plans to hold another planting day in the fall.
passages.p27: For decades, students have been told that a four-year degree is the only reliable path to a good career. That advice deserves a second look. Many skilled trades, such as electrician, plumber and welder, offer paid apprenticeships in which workers earn a wage while they train. People who finish these programs often have no student debt and hold a license that employers want. None of this means college is a poor choice; for many careers, it remains essential. The point is that students should weigh every option instead of following a single script.
passages.p28: In summer, leaves are green because they are packed with chlorophyll, the pigment plants use to capture sunlight. Leaves also contain yellow and orange pigments, but the large amount of chlorophyll hides them. As the days grow shorter in autumn, many trees stop making chlorophyll, and the green fades. The yellow and orange that were there all along begin to show. Some trees also produce new red pigments in the fall, especially when the days are sunny and the nights are cool.
passages.p29: To all shift supervisors: Starting next month, overtime must be approved in writing by a department manager before the shift begins. In the past, overtime was often approved after it had already been worked, which made it hard to stay within the quarterly budget. Supervisors with urgent staffing needs should contact the on-call manager, who can approve overtime by email at any hour. Overtime worked without approval will still be paid, but it may result in a written warning for the supervisor.
passages.p30: Before 1869, a trip from the East Coast to California could take months by wagon or by ship. That changed when two railroad companies, one building east from Sacramento and one building west from Omaha, met at Promontory Summit, Utah. The Central Pacific relied heavily on thousands of Chinese immigrant workers, who blasted tunnels through the Sierra Nevada mountains under dangerous conditions. Once the line was finished, the journey across the country took about a week. The railroad sped the movement of people and goods, but it also brought settlers onto the lands of Native American nations, leading to conflict.
passages.p31: Many teenagers keep their phones beside the bed at night. Researchers have found that light from screens can delay the body's release of melatonin, a hormone that signals it is time to sleep. Notifications can also wake a sleeper or tempt them to check messages. One simple change is to charge the phone in another room. Students who try it often report falling asleep faster, though they may need a regular alarm clock to wake up on time.
passages.p32: Marcus checked the forecast twice before leaving and packed his heaviest jacket, gloves and an extra pair of socks. At the trailhead, he signed the hikers' log, writing down his planned route and the time he expected to return. Halfway up the mountain, the sky turned gray and the first flakes began to fall. Marcus looked at his watch, looked at the clouds and turned back toward the parking lot.
passages.p33: The city's new bus app promised to make commuting easier, but so far it has mostly added frustration. Arrival times are often wrong by ten minutes or more, and the app freezes when riders try to buy a ticket. Officials say an update is coming. Until it arrives, riders would be wise to leave a few minutes early and keep a few dollars in cash.
passages.p34: Many beginners believe the fastest way to get stronger is to exercise hard every single day. In fact, muscles grow stronger during recovery, not during the workout itself. Hard exercise causes tiny amounts of damage to muscle fibers; during rest, the body repairs them and builds them back slightly stronger. Training without enough rest can lead to fatigue, poor performance and injury. For this reason, most training programs alternate hard days with easier days or complete rest.
passages.p35: Some people argue that schools should require every student to learn a second language, because it builds communication skills and opens doors to more jobs. Others respond that class time is limited and that students would gain more from extra math or reading. Both sides agree that learning a language has value. They disagree about whether it should be required.
passages.p36: The hardware store's records show that snow shovel sales rose sharply in the first week of December, then dropped almost to zero by mid-January, even though snow kept falling. The manager suspects that most households buy only one shovel each winter, usually right after the first big storm.

questions.question: The main idea of the passage is that:
choices: people working in the heat should drink water regularly to avoid dehydration
sweating is the only way the body cools itself
dark yellow urine is a sign of serious illness
people should avoid salt in hot weather
questions.explanation:
The passage explains how sweating causes water loss and ends with its main advice: drink water at regular intervals. The other choices either overstate a detail or are not mentioned.
Tip: the main idea is often in the first or last sentence.

questions.question: According to the passage, sweat cools the body by:
choices: evaporating and carrying heat away
adding salt to the skin
slowing the heart rate
causing thirst
questions.explanation: The second sentence states it directly: "As sweat evaporates from the skin, it carries heat away."

questions.question: Why does the passage advise drinking water before feeling thirsty?
choices: Thirst may not appear until the body already needs water
Drinking water stops all sweating
Thirst only happens at night
Salt prevents thirst
questions.explanation: The passage says "thirst often lags behind the body's actual need," meaning you are already low on water by the time you feel thirsty.

questions.question: According to the passage, how long did the Pony Express operate?
choices: About eighteen months
About ten days
About ten years
About two months
questions.explanation: The passage states "the service lasted only about eighteen months." Ten days was how long a letter took to cross the route.

questions.question: The passage suggests that the Pony Express closed mainly because:
choices: a much faster way to send messages became available
the riders refused to keep working
horses became too expensive
stagecoaches were faster
questions.explanation: The passage connects the closing to the completed telegraph, which could send messages "in minutes." It also notes the service was never profitable. Stagecoaches were slower, not faster.

questions.question: As used in the passage, the word profitable most nearly means:
choices: making money
famous
dangerous
fast
questions.explanation: Profitable means bringing in more money than it costs. "Never profitable" means the business always lost money.

questions.question: Which statement best expresses the main idea of the passage?
choices: Smoke detectors protect people only if they are kept in working order
Most house fires start at night
Smoke detectors should be replaced every month
Fire officials install detectors in most homes
questions.explanation: The key sentence is "Smoke detectors give early warning, but only if they work," and the rest explains how to keep them working. The passage says to test them monthly, not replace them monthly.

questions.question: According to the passage, how often should the entire smoke detector be replaced?
choices: Every ten years
Every year
Every month
After every fire
questions.explanation: The passage says to replace "the entire unit every ten years." Batteries are replaced yearly, and the detector is tested monthly. Read carefully which item each number goes with.

questions.question: The last sentence of the passage suggests that many people:
choices: do not maintain their smoke detectors properly
test their detectors every month
have no smoke detectors at all
have more detectors than they need
questions.explanation: If "many homes have at least one detector that does not work," then many people are not testing their detectors or replacing the batteries.

questions.question: The author's main purpose is to:
choices: encourage adults to start learning a new language
explain how children learn pronunciation
argue that grammar is not important
compare two different languages
questions.explanation: The author challenges the belief that only children can learn languages, lists adult advantages, and ends with "Age … is a poor excuse for not starting." That is encouragement aimed at adults.

questions.question: According to the passage, children have an advantage over adults in:
choices: pronunciation
grammar
memory techniques
early progress
questions.explanation: "Young children pick up pronunciation more easily." Grammar, memory techniques, and faster early progress are listed as adult advantages.

questions.question: By calling age "a poor excuse," the author suggests that:
choices: age should not stop an adult from learning a language
adults make too many excuses at work
children learn faster in every way
most adults already speak two languages
questions.explanation: A poor excuse is a weak reason for not doing something. The author means age is not a good reason to avoid learning a language.

questions.question: The main idea of the passage is that:
choices: honeybees are most valuable to people as pollinators of crops
honeybees make honey from pollen
farmers raise bees mainly to sell honey
almonds are the most important crop
questions.explanation: The first sentence sets it up: bees' "greatest value … lies elsewhere" than honey. The rest explains that value: pollinating crops.

questions.question: Based on the passage, farmers rent hives during the blooming season because:
choices: the bees help the crops produce fruit
they want to sell the honey
the bees protect flowers from other insects
hives are cheaper in the spring
questions.explanation: The passage says crops depend on bee pollination to produce fruit and seeds, and the last sentence begins "For this reason," linking the hive rentals to pollination.

questions.question: According to the passage, declination is:
choices: the difference between magnetic north and true north
the direction of the North Pole
a type of military map
the distance covered on a long march
questions.explanation: "The difference between the two, called declination …" — the two being magnetic north and true north.

questions.question: As used in the passage, the word bearing most nearly means:
choices: direction
weight
behavior
patience
questions.explanation: In navigation, a bearing is the direction you travel, measured as an angle on a compass. Bearing can mean other things (such as how someone carries themselves), but context here is about navigation.

questions.question: The passage implies that ignoring declination causes the biggest errors when a person:
choices: travels a long distance
reads a small map
walks at night
uses a new compass
questions.explanation: The last sentence says ignoring declination can put you "hundreds of meters off course over a long march." A small angle error grows the farther you go.

questions.question: Which statement best summarizes the passage?
choices: Getting enough sleep on a regular schedule matters for health and safety
Sleeping late on weekends makes up for lost sleep
Most accidents happen on weekends
Adults need more sleep than children
questions.explanation: The passage lists the dangers of short sleep and recommends a consistent schedule. It directly says weekend sleep does not fully make up for lost sleep, so the second choice is wrong.

questions.question: What do experts recommend, according to the passage?
choices: Going to bed and waking up at about the same time every day
Sleeping late on weekends
Sleeping no more than seven hours
Taking naps at work
questions.explanation: The last sentence: "Experts recommend going to bed and waking up at about the same time every day, even on days off."

questions.question: According to the notice, what must a driver do if a vehicle is damaged?
choices: Report it on Form 12 before leaving the lot
Return the vehicle with a full tank
Sign the vehicle out after 0800
Wait thirty days before driving again
questions.explanation: "Any damage must be reported on Form 12 before the driver leaves the lot." Note the fuel rule is half a tank, not a full tank.

questions.question: The main purpose of the notice is to:
choices: explain new rules for using vehicles
announce the opening of a motor pool
describe how to repair vehicles
list drivers who lost their privileges
questions.explanation: Everything in the notice is a rule about signing out, fueling, and reporting damage, plus the penalty for breaking those rules.

questions.question: What happens to drivers who do not follow the procedures?
choices: They lose vehicle privileges for thirty days
They must pay for a full tank of fuel
They must fill out Form 12
They must report on Monday
questions.explanation: The last sentence states the penalty: "Drivers who do not follow these procedures will lose vehicle privileges for thirty days."

questions.question: According to the passage, why do you see lightning before you hear thunder?
choices: Light travels faster than sound
Thunder forms after the lightning is over
The flash is closer to you than the sound
Ears react more slowly than eyes
questions.explanation: "Because light travels much faster than sound, you see the flash before you hear the thunder."

questions.question: Using the method in the passage, if you count 15 seconds between the flash and the thunder, about how far away is the strike?
choices: 3 miles
5 miles
15 miles
75 miles
questions.explanation: The passage says to divide the seconds by five: 15 ÷ 5 = 3 miles. Since 15 seconds is less than 30, the storm is also close enough to be dangerous.

questions.question: Based on the passage, the Navajo language made a good code mainly because:
choices: few people outside the Navajo community understood it
it was easy to write down
machines could translate it quickly
the enemy already used it
questions.explanation: The passage says the language "had no written form and was spoken by very few outsiders," so the enemy had no way to learn it.

questions.question: As used in the passage, decode most nearly means:
choices: turn a coded message back into plain language
write a new message
send a message by radio
break a promise
questions.explanation: To encode is to put a message into code; to decode is to turn it back into ordinary language. The prefix de- means to reverse or undo.

questions.question: Which statement best expresses the main idea of the passage?
choices: Navajo code talkers gave the Marines a fast and secure way to send messages
Machines were the fastest way to send wartime messages
The Navajo language was invented during World War II
The Marine Corps created a new written language
questions.explanation: The passage describes the need for secure messages, how the Navajo code met it, its speed, and that it was never broken. The language already existed; it was not invented for the war.

questions.question: The author's main purpose is to:
choices: warn readers about the cost of carrying a credit card balance
convince readers never to use credit cards
explain how to apply for a credit card
compare interest rates at different banks
questions.explanation: The author calls cards "a useful tool," so they are not saying never use them. The focus is the expense of carrying a balance and how to avoid it.

questions.question: According to the passage, how can a cardholder avoid interest charges entirely?
choices: Pay the full balance every month
Pay the minimum every month
Keep the balance under $1,000
Use the card only once a year
questions.explanation: The last sentence: "Paying the full balance every month avoids interest charges entirely." Paying only the minimum is what makes debt expensive.

questions.question: According to the passage, a warm-up:
choices: raises body temperature and increases blood flow to the muscles
guarantees that no injury will happen
can replace the workout itself
lowers the heart rate before exercise
questions.explanation: The first sentence says this directly. Note the passage says a warm-up "may reduce the risk of injury," not that it guarantees safety.

questions.question: The passage suggests that advice about stretching before exercise:
choices: has changed over time
has always been the same
was never widely followed
is required by law
questions.explanation: Long stretches were "once standard advice" but are "now considered less useful," which shows the advice has changed.

questions.question: The main idea of the passage is that:
choices: recycling aluminum saves energy, and the metal can be reused many times
aluminum cans are made from raw ore
recycled cans take years to return to stores
new cans are better quality than recycled cans
questions.explanation: All three sentences describe benefits of recycling aluminum: energy savings, no loss of quality, and quick reuse. The passage says recycled aluminum does not lose quality.

questions.question: According to the passage, recycling an aluminum can saves about how much of the energy needed to make a new can from ore?
choices: 95 percent
60 percent
50 percent
2 percent
questions.explanation: The first sentence states "about 95 percent."

questions.question: The author's attitude toward volunteer firefighters is best described as:
choices: admiring
critical
uninterested
amused
questions.explanation: The author praises their sacrifice and says their dedication "deserves far more recognition." Those are words of admiration.

questions.question: According to the passage, volunteer firefighters:
choices: receive little or no pay
are trained by paid fire departments
answer calls only during the day
mostly live in large cities
questions.explanation: "They receive little or no pay." The passage says they answer calls "at all hours" and serve small towns.

questions.question: As used in the passage, dedication most nearly means:
choices: commitment
payment
training
location
questions.explanation: Dedication means devotion or commitment to a task or cause, shown here by leaving jobs and families to answer calls.

questions.question: According to the passage, where can a driver find the correct tire pressure?
choices: On a sticker inside the driver's door
On the side of the tire
In the owner's monthly bill
At any gas station
questions.explanation: "The correct pressure is listed on a sticker inside the driver's door." The number on the tire is the maximum, not the recommended pressure.

questions.question: Based on the passage, a driver who fills tires to the number printed on the tire would most likely:
choices: put in more air than recommended
put in exactly the recommended amount
underinflate the tires
damage the door sticker
questions.explanation: The tire shows the maximum pressure it can safely hold. Since that is higher than the recommended pressure, filling to it means using more air than recommended.

questions.question: According to the passage, bamboo is a type of:
choices: grass
tree
vine
fern
questions.explanation: "Despite its treelike height, bamboo is actually a type of grass." The word despite signals a surprising fact: it looks like a tree but is not.

questions.question: Which statement best summarizes the passage?
choices: Bamboo is a fast-growing, strong grass that is widely used for building
Bamboo is used only to make furniture
Bamboo is the tallest tree in Asia
Most buildings in Asia are made entirely of bamboo
questions.explanation: The passage covers bamboo's fast growth, that it is a grass, and its use as a building material. The other choices are too narrow, incorrect, or exaggerated.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: Maria saved money carefully so she could buy a car
Maria liked packing her own lunch
Maria's job paid very well
Maria bought a brand-new car
questions.explanation: Every sentence is about how Maria saved for a car. Watch the details: she bought a used car, not a new one.

questions.question: According to the passage, how did Maria save money?
choices: She put half of each paycheck into savings
She borrowed money from her parents
She sold her old bike
She worked a second job
questions.explanation: The second sentence says she put half of her paycheck into a savings account each week. The other choices are never mentioned.

questions.question: According to the passage, why do dogs pant?
choices: To cool down
Because they are hungry
To show they are angry
To clean their teeth
questions.explanation: The first sentence answers it directly: "Dogs pant to cool down."

questions.question: According to the passage, how are dogs different from people?
choices: Dogs have far fewer sweat glands in their skin
Dogs do not need water
Dogs cannot feel heat
Dogs sweat more than people
questions.explanation: "Unlike people, dogs have very few sweat glands in their skin." The word unlike signals a difference.

questions.question: When will the library open again?
choices: Tuesday at 9:00 a.m.
Monday at 9:00 a.m.
Tuesday at noon
Wednesday morning
questions.explanation: "It will open again on Tuesday at 9:00 a.m." Monday is the day it is closed.

questions.question: A person has a book due on Monday and returns it on Tuesday. What will most likely happen?
choices: They won't pay a late fee
They will pay a late fee
They will lose their library card
They will have to buy the book
questions.explanation: The last sentence says books due Monday may be returned Tuesday without a late fee.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly doing?
choices: Correcting a false belief about bats and explaining how they find food
Warning that bats are dangerous
Describing where bats live
Arguing that bats should be protected
questions.explanation: It opens with a myth ("bats are blind"), says it isn't true, then explains echolocation. Nothing is said about danger, habitats or protection.

questions.question: As used in the passage, echolocation means:
choices: Finding things by listening to echoes
Seeing in the dark with special eyes
Flying very fast
Sleeping upside down
questions.explanation: The passage defines it right after the colon: bats make sounds and listen for the echoes. Definitions often follow a colon or a comma.

questions.question: Why did Sergeant Lee tell the recruits to drink water before they were thirsty?
choices: Feeling thirsty means the body is already low on water
The march would be very short
The water was about to run out
Drinking water makes people march faster
questions.explanation: Her own words explain it: "By the time you feel thirsty, your body is already low on water."

questions.question: Who gave the advice about drinking water?
choices: Sergeant Lee
The recruits
A doctor
A captain
questions.explanation: The first sentence says Sergeant Lee told the recruits. The recruits received the advice; they didn't give it.

questions.question: What is the author's main purpose?
choices: To persuade readers to wear seat belts
To explain how cars are built
To describe a specific crash
To compare different cars
questions.explanation: The passage gives reasons to buckle up and points out how easy it is. Giving reasons to do something is persuading.

questions.question: According to the passage, a seat belt keeps you from:
choices: Being thrown against the dashboard or out of the vehicle
Driving too fast
Getting a ticket
Running out of gas
questions.explanation: The second sentence lists exactly these two dangers.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: Honey can last a very long time without spoiling
Honey is made by bees
Honey should be kept in the refrigerator
Bacteria are good for honey
questions.explanation: The passage is about why honey almost never spoils. "Made by bees" is true, but the passage never says it, so it can't be the main idea.

questions.question: According to the passage, why doesn't honey spoil easily?
choices: Its low water content and acidity make it hard for bacteria to grow
It is kept cold
Bees add preservatives
It is cooked before it is sold
questions.explanation: The second sentence gives both reasons: very little water and natural acidity.

questions.question: According to the notice, what must guests do?
choices: Sign in at the front desk
Pay a fee
Show two forms of ID
Arrive before 5:00 a.m.
questions.explanation: "Guests must be at least 16 years old and must sign in at the front desk." A fee and IDs are never mentioned.

questions.question: A service member wants to bring a 14-year-old cousin to the gym. Based on the notice:
choices: The cousin can't come as a guest
The cousin can come after signing in
The cousin can come after 10:00 p.m.
The cousin can come with a second guest
questions.explanation: Guests must be at least 16, so a 14-year-old can't be a guest, even after signing in.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: Practicing helped Kevin pass his driving test
Kevin's uncle teaches driving for a living
Kevin never uses his turn signal
Driving tests are too hard
questions.explanation: Kevin failed, practiced for a month and then passed easily. The passage is about practice paying off.

questions.question: According to the passage, why did Kevin fail his first driving test?
choices: He didn't signal before changing lanes
He drove too fast
He hit a curb
He arrived late
questions.explanation: The first sentence says he "forgot to signal before changing lanes."

questions.question: According to the passage, the new trees will help:
choices: Keep soil from washing away
Lower taxes
Bring in tourists
Reduce traffic
questions.explanation: The passage lists two benefits: shade in summer, and keeping soil from washing away when it rains.

questions.question: As used in the passage, provide most nearly means:
choices: Give
Take away
Sell
Hide
questions.explanation: The trees will provide shade, meaning they will give shade. Test it by swapping the word in: "The trees will give shade."

questions.question: What is the author's main purpose?
choices: To encourage students to consider more than one path after high school
To argue that college is a waste of money
To explain how to become a licensed electrician
To criticize skilled trades for low pay
questions.explanation: The author questions the idea that a degree is the only path, then says college "remains essential" for many careers. The last sentence states the point: "weigh every option." The second choice is a trap: the author says outright that college is not a poor choice.

questions.question: The author would most likely agree with which statement?
choices: The best choice depends on a student's career goals
Every student should become an apprentice
A four-year degree always leads to debt
Skilled trades require no training
questions.explanation: The author says college is essential for many careers but trades fit others, so the right path depends on the goal. The wrong choices use extreme words (every, always, no) that the passage doesn't support.

questions.question: As used in the passage, script most nearly means:
choices: A fixed plan everyone is expected to follow
Handwriting
A movie screenplay
A doctor's prescription
questions.explanation: "Following a single script" means doing what everyone is told to do, as if reading lines. The more common meanings (a screenplay, a prescription) don't fit this sentence.

questions.question: According to the passage, the yellow color in autumn leaves:
choices: Was in the leaves all summer, hidden by the green
Is made only after the first frost
Comes from minerals in the soil
Appears because leaves absorb more sunlight in fall
questions.explanation: "The yellow and orange that were there all along begin to show." Frost and soil are never mentioned.

questions.question: Based on the passage, an autumn with mostly cloudy days and warm nights would most likely produce:
choices: Fewer bright red leaves
More chlorophyll in the leaves
No yellow leaves at all
Leaves that stay green all winter
questions.explanation: The passage says red pigments form "especially when the days are sunny and the nights are cool." Cloudy days and warm nights are the opposite, so expect less red. The yellow is already in the leaves, so it would still show.

questions.question: Which title best fits the passage?
choices: Why Leaves Change Color in Autumn
How Trees Grow Taller
The Dangers of an Early Frost
Why Plants Need Water
questions.explanation: Every sentence explains where autumn leaf colors come from. A good title covers the whole passage, not one detail.

questions.question: According to the memo, what is the main reason for the new overtime rule?
choices: To keep overtime spending within the budget
To stop paying for overtime
To punish workers who stay late
To reduce the number of supervisors
questions.explanation: The memo says approving overtime after the fact "made it hard to stay within the quarterly budget." It also says unapproved overtime will still be paid, so the second choice is wrong.

questions.question: A worker stays two hours late without approval. Based on the memo, what will most likely happen?
choices: The worker will be paid, but the supervisor may get a warning
The worker will not be paid for the extra hours
The worker will receive a written warning
The hours will count only if a manager signs off later
questions.explanation: The memo says unapproved overtime "will still be paid" and the warning goes to the supervisor, not the worker. Read carefully who each rule applies to.

questions.question: How can a supervisor get overtime approved for an urgent need?
choices: Contact the on-call manager, who can approve it by email
Wait until the next month
Approve it after the shift is over
Have the workers sign a form
questions.explanation: "Supervisors with urgent staffing needs should contact the on-call manager, who can approve overtime by email at any hour."

questions.question: Which statement best expresses the main idea of the passage?
choices: The first transcontinental railroad changed travel across the country, with costs as well as benefits
Chinese immigrant workers built every railroad in the United States
Ships were faster than wagons for crossing the country
Utah became the center of American trade after 1869
questions.explanation: The passage covers how much faster travel became, who built the railroad, and the conflict it brought. The main idea has to include both the benefits and the costs. The second choice goes too far: the passage is about one railroad, not every railroad.

questions.question: As used in the passage, relied heavily on most nearly means:
choices: Depended greatly on
Leaned against
Paid little attention to
Argued with
questions.explanation: The company depended on thousands of Chinese workers to do the dangerous work. Swap in the choice to check: "The Central Pacific depended greatly on thousands of … workers."

questions.question: The author's attitude toward the railroad is best described as:
choices: Balanced, noting both benefits and harms
Entirely celebratory
Strongly opposed
Uninterested
questions.explanation: The author praises the faster travel and trade, but also points out dangerous working conditions and conflict with Native American nations. A tone question asks about the whole passage, not one sentence.

questions.question: Why might students who charge their phones in another room need a regular alarm clock?
choices: Many people use their phone as an alarm
Alarm clocks help the body make melatonin
Phones can't be charged overnight
Phones stop working when moved
questions.explanation: The passage doesn't say it directly, but if the phone is in another room, an alarm on it may not wake you. You have to connect that to how people commonly use their phones.

questions.question: What is the author's main purpose?
choices: To suggest a simple way to sleep better
To explain how phones are built
To argue that teenagers shouldn't own phones
To describe how melatonin is made in a lab
questions.explanation: The passage explains why phones can disturb sleep and offers one simple fix. It never says teenagers shouldn't have phones.

questions.question: As used in the passage, tempt most nearly means:
choices: Make someone want to do something
Force someone to do something
Warn someone about something
Stop someone from doing something
questions.explanation: Notifications tempt sleepers to check messages: they make them want to, without forcing them.

questions.question: Based on his actions, Marcus can best be described as:
choices: Cautious and well prepared
Careless
Lost
In a hurry to reach the top
questions.explanation: He checked the forecast twice, packed warm gear, logged his route and turned back when snow started. Every action shows caution and planning.

questions.question: Why did Marcus most likely write his route in the hikers' log?
choices: So searchers would know where to look if he didn't return
Because the log is where hikers pay their fee
To show other hikers how far he planned to go
To remember the way back to his car
questions.explanation: He wrote his route and expected return time, the information others would need to find him. The passage never mentions a fee, and he wouldn't need a log at the trailhead to find his way back.

questions.question: Which statement is most likely true?
choices: Marcus decided the weather made it unsafe to keep going
Marcus reached the top of the mountain
Marcus forgot to bring warm clothes
Marcus turned back because he was afraid of heights
questions.explanation: He checked his watch and the clouds as snow began, then turned back. That points to a decision about the weather and the time. The passage says he packed warm clothes and mentions no fear of heights.

questions.question: The author's attitude toward the new bus app is best described as:
choices: Critical
Enthusiastic
Neutral
Amused
questions.explanation: Words like "mostly added frustration," "often wrong" and "freezes" show a critical attitude.

questions.question: Why does the author suggest that riders keep some cash?
choices: Buying a ticket in the app may not work
Buses no longer accept the app
Cash fares are cheaper than app fares
The update will remove ticket sales from the app
questions.explanation: The passage says the app "freezes when riders try to buy a ticket." Cash is a backup. The other choices aren't stated anywhere in the passage.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: The new bus app has problems, so riders should plan around them for now
Officials have already fixed the app
City buses are always late
Riders should stop taking the bus
questions.explanation: The passage describes the app's problems and gives temporary advice until the update. The update is only promised, not done, and nothing suggests giving up the bus.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: Rest is an important part of getting stronger
Beginners should not exercise at all
Exercise permanently damages muscles
All training programs are the same
questions.explanation: The passage explains that muscles get stronger while recovering and that most programs build in rest. The damage it mentions is tiny and gets repaired, so permanent damage is wrong.

questions.question: A recruit lifts weights hard every day and feels weaker each week. Based on the passage, what is the most likely explanation?
choices: Not enough recovery time between workouts
Too much rest between workouts
Lifting too little weight
Exercising on the wrong days of the week
questions.explanation: The passage says training without enough rest leads to fatigue and poor performance. Hard work every day leaves no time for repair.

questions.question: As used in the passage, alternate most nearly means:
choices: Switch back and forth between
Cancel
Combine into one
Repeat exactly
questions.explanation: Programs alternate hard days with easy days: hard, easy, hard, easy.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the passage?
choices: To present two sides of a debate
To prove that language classes are useless
To argue that math matters more than any other subject
To explain how to learn a second language
questions.explanation: The passage gives one side's argument, then the other's, and says where they agree and disagree. It doesn't take a side, so it is presenting a debate, not making an argument.

questions.question: On what do both sides agree?
choices: Learning a language has value
Every student should be required to take a language
Math is more important than reading
The school day should be longer
questions.explanation: "Both sides agree that learning a language has value." They disagree about whether it should be required, so the second choice is only one side's view.

questions.question: As used in the passage, respond most nearly means:
choices: Answer
Ignore
Agree completely
Repeat
questions.explanation: Others respond means they answer the first argument with one of their own.

questions.question: Why did shovel sales drop in mid-January even though it was still snowing?
choices: Most households had already bought a shovel
The store ran out of shovels
Shovel prices went up
Customers started using snowblowers
questions.explanation: The manager suspects most households buy one shovel each winter, after the first big storm. Once they own one, they stop buying. The other choices may sound reasonable, but the passage gives no support for them.

questions.question: The word suspects suggests that the manager:
choices: Believes this explanation but isn't certain
Has proven the explanation with data
Disagrees with the explanation
Is accusing customers of something
questions.explanation: To suspect something is to think it's likely true without proof. In this context it isn't about accusing anyone. Words like suspects, suggests and may signal a guess, not a fact.
